claim: Business and Professions Code Section 16600 The bedrock of California's employment law is codified in California Business and Professions Code section 16600, which explicitly states that "every contract by which anyone is restrained from engaging in a lawful profession, trade, or business of any kind is to that extent void"
evidence: With few exceptions, Section 16600 provides that “every contract by which anyone is restrained from engaging in a lawful profession, trade, or business of any kind is to that extent void.”
excerpt:
Senate Bill 699 and Assembly Bill 1076, signed into law by Gov. Gavin Newsom, further strengthen the current protections under Section 16600 of the Business and Professions Code. More specifically, they expand the ways employees can challenge noncompetes and require employers to provide noncompete notices to their employees. With few exceptions, Section 16600 provides that “every contract by which anyone is restrained from engaging in a lawful profession, trade, or business of any kind is to that extent void.”
